chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ajlan Abu Salih, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you arrive at the Well of Maymoun or the Well of Abdul Samad, perform ghusl, take off your sandals, walk barefoot, and maintain tranquility and dignity.'

key_terms.بِئْرِ عَبْدِ الصَّمَدِ: Well of Abdul Samad, another location associated with entering Mecca
key_terms.بِئْرِ مَيْمُونٍ: Well of Maymoun, a specific location associated with entering Mecca

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended rituals and etiquette upon entering Mecca according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual preparation for entering the sacred precincts of Mecca, linking physical purification with inner composure. The specific mention of the Well of Maymoun (Birr Ma'yun) and the Well of Abdul Samad anchors the practice in the historical geography of the Prophet's era, while the emphasis on 'sakinah' and 'waqar' reflects the Shia scholarly focus on embodying reverence during the transition into the holy city.
